title: The History and Future of Social Technologies

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The History and Future of Social Technologies restores institutions to technological history.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Tools expand capability, while rules and shared expectations determine what that capability means.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The book follows their interaction through money, law, organizations, science, and digital systems.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Its central criterion is how arrangements detect mistakes and permit their own revision.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Readers gain a vocabulary for the less visible machinery shaping every visible invention.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Money appears to reside in objects or numbers until the supporting promises begin to fail.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Records, shared expectations, settlement, and enforcement help make the familiar object usable.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The book calls these configurations social technologies because they can be transmitted and revised.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Their participants interpret rules, so the arrangement is not a machine of obedient gears.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: This example opens a history of coordination that hardware alone cannot explain.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The historical journey follows how material systems reshape institutions and institutions shape technical development.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: A rule can become ineffective when the surrounding infrastructure or balance of power changes.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Greater scale can improve coordination while making local consequences harder to hear.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The recurring test is whether the arrangement preserves information and authority needed for correction.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: AI enters this history as new capability whose social meaning remains a governing problem.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Begin with the missing half of technological history and the definition of social technology.
